newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
All Papers
PRIYANKA GANDHI WEDS ROBERT VADRA

Priyanka Gandhi, daughter of assassinated prime minister Rajiv Gandhi and heiress of India's leading political family, was married to Robert Vadra in a private ceremony held amid tight security. President Shankar Dayal Sharma, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Vice-President K.R. Narayanan were among the wedding guests, most of whom were family friends.
The Times Of India
LEFT WANTS FOOD SUBSIDY

Left parties and representatives of the United Front government clashed over increasing food subsidies. The Left maintained the government must honour its commitment in the common minimum programme (CMP) to the new public distribution system. However, the Finance Minister pointed out the CMP was also committed to reining in the fiscal deficit. The meeting focussed on increase in prices of foodgrains and price rise in general, reserving a discussion on other contentious issues for February 20, when the steering committee would meet again.
Indian Express
TOUGH BILL ON MONEY LAUNDERING IN OFFING

The Finance Ministry was giving final touches to extremely tough legislation which would make it a crime to launder proceeds from any criminal acts including bank frauds, smuggling, terrorism, bribes and other acts of corruption. The legislation is likely to be tabled in the budget session of parliament.
The Hindustan Times
CPP'S ADVICE MUST BEFORE TOPPLING GOVERNMENT

Members of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) executive told the party chief that they expected to be consulted before a decision was taken to topple the government. At a meeting of the CPP executive they said party members were critical of the government and were happy that the Congress had decided to put it on tenterhooks.
The Economic Times
STERLING CLIPS FOREIGN OFFERING TO $175 MLN

Sterling Computers, part of the Essar group of companies, decided to prune the value of shares it planned to offer to foreign investors by 40 percent. The total offering was slashed to $175 million from $300 million. The company, however, did not reduce the number of shares to be placed, which stayed at the earlier level of 4.8 million. The shares on offer account for 49 percent of the total equity of the company.
$500 MLN DEBT ISSUE ON CARDS

Reliance Industries (RIL) was holding a letter of comfort from its investment bankers for raising another $500 million of debt for maturities between 10 and 30 years from international investors. The company has already raised $914 million through the debt route in the last one-and-a-half years.
CORPORATES NEGOTIATING TO PIERCE SOVEREIGN CEILING

Leading Indian corporates, including Reliance Industries, were attempting to pierce the sovereign ceiling using the structured obligation route in forthcoming overseas bond placements. The corporates suggested setting up an interest payment reserve account overseas where a part of the loan proceeds could be deposited.
MITTALS TO CONVERT NIPPON DENRO STAKE INTO NRI EQUITY

The Mittals of the Ispat group were converting their equity into non-resident Indian (NRI) equity in Nippon Denro Ispat. The company would issue fully convertible debentures on a rights basis, aggregating eight billion rupees, with 1:2 ratio. After this, NRI and foreign equity in the company would go up to 66 percent from the existing 13 percent. Sources said the Mittal group would be increasing their stake to 40 percent from the existing 5.58 percent, thus, bringing in 3.84 billion rupees in the company.
Financial Express
RE-RATE ORIENTAL BANK SCRIP, SAYS I-SEC

ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) made a strong case for re-rating the Oriental Bank of Commerce's (OBC) stocks. It also said that the premia enjoyed by the newly listed private sector banks were unsustainable and the valuations would reflect that fact in the long run. The I-Sec research report forecast OBC's operating earning per share to grow by 22 percent in the current fiscal and by 15 percent in 1997/98 (April-March).
SWAP RATIO SET FOR CYANAMID, WYETH MERGER

Shareholders in Wyeth Laboratories would receive three equity shares of Cyanamid India for every two shares held in a two-step restructuring of the U.S. firm American Home Products Corporation's Indian operations. Cyanamid would also transfer its agricultural products business into a separate company. Its shareholders would receive one share in the new agro entity for every share held in Cyanamid India. The merger was a fallout of the $10.7 billion acquisition of American Cyanamid Company by American Home Products Corporation in 1994.
Business Standard
INCENTIVES PACKAGE FOR POWER PROJECTS IN MAHARASHTRA

The Maharashtra government unveiled a package of incentives for the seven independent power projects (IPPs), tenders for which were floated by the state power board (MSEB). The incentives include concessional sales tax and tax exemption on sale of electricity. The state's energy secretary, said tariff was the main criterion for awarding the projects.
CORPORATES JITTERY OVER TAKEOVER CODE

Indian corporates voiced their apprehension over the new takeover code, even as the bourse regulator (SEBI) prepared to submit it to the government for notification. The new code was likely to be notified on February 20, 1997. Industrialists expressed fear of existing managements being usurped by foreign predators since the code did not provide adequate safeguards to ward off such threats. There was a feeling in government that industrialists were trying to buy time by tying up the takeover code with the implementation of the new Companies Act.
Business Line
HIKE IN RAILWAY OUTLAY RULED OUT

The Finance Ministry ruled out any enhancement in the annual plan outlay for the railways in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). With the outlay pegged at 83 billion rupees, the plan investment was likely to register a decline of seven percent in nominal terms. This would translate into a 17 percent drop in real terms. Sources said in view of the overall resource crunch, the railways were told that additional funds, if any, would be provided only at the revised estimate stage. The railways had sought a plan size of 110 billion rupees and 33 billion rupees in budgetary support.
